course.title: Metrics, Semantic Models and Dashboards
course.tagline: Define each number once, model it, show it to the person who decides, and test the agent that answers questions about it
course.description: Participants take over performance reporting for Wadi Noor Transit, a fictional bus operator whose three reports give three different on-time figures. On a synthetic warehouse of trips, boardings and routes they write governed metric definitions, build a semantic model that defines each metric once, design a dashboard for one decision within a load-time budget, trace an anomaly to its source, and test a conversational analytics agent on certified questions with and without the semantic layer. Platform-scale semantic layer design is DS-408.
course.audience: Practitioners. Data scientists and analysts who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: an analysis they framed, carried out and explained to a stakeholder.
prerequisites: Writes SQL with joins, grouping and window functions
Has built a chart-based report for others
course.format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

outcomes.text: Explain why reports built on one warehouse disagree on the same measure, given three operator reports with different on-time figures
outcomes.evidence: a diagnosis naming the definitional cause of each difference

outcomes.text: Draft metric definitions stating formula, grain, filters, time logic, owner and limits, given twelve business questions and the data dictionary
outcomes.evidence: a metric catalogue that passes a peer checklist and reconciles to source totals

outcomes.text: Implement a star-schema semantic model with a slowly changing route dimension and each metric defined once, given the synthetic transit warehouse
outcomes.evidence: reference values returned for 25 test queries

outcomes.text: Analyse a metric anomaly by drill-down and segmentation to find its source, given a seeded drop in weekly ridership
outcomes.evidence: an anomaly note naming the cause, affected segments and correction

outcomes.text: Design a dashboard for a named audience and decision within a load-time budget, given the operations director's brief and a three-second budget
outcomes.evidence: a dashboard, a one-page rationale and recorded timings, scored on a rubric

outcomes.text: Evaluate a conversational analytics agent against governed metrics and decide which question types it may answer unreviewed, given 40 certified questions and a stated tolerance for wrong figures
outcomes.evidence: a memo with accuracy by question type and configuration, plausible wrong answers and a go or no-go decision

case_study.name: Wadi Noor Transit
case_study.summary: A fictional city bus operator with twelve routes from three depots, whose operations, planning and board reports give three different on-time figures for the same month. A synthetic warehouse (January to October 2026, fixed seed) holds about 85,000 trips, 329,000 timepoint arrivals, 849,000 card taps, 2,400 complaints and 121,000 fare sales, with planted problems for every session.

capstone.summary: Catalogue, semantic model, dashboard and agent memo for a second subject area (fares and concessions), in a public repository whose README reports measured query accuracy and load times, defended in a ten-minute review
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository for the fares and concessions area: the metric catalogue, the Apache Ossie model with its test queries, the dashboard with its one-page rationale, the agent memo, and a README that reports the measured query accuracy and the load times and says how to rerun them.
